import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_5/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_5/training_1.csv"

df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# According to operation_history: JOIN on ProvinciaID
# Source0 schema: ['ComunaID', 'ComunaNombre', 'ProvinciaID']
# Source1 schema: ['ProvinciaID', 'ProvinciaNombre', 'RegionID']

# Perform inner join on ProvinciaID
df_joined = pd.merge(df_source0, df_source1, on="ProvinciaID", how="inner")

# Reorder and select columns to match target schema:
# Target schema: ['ProvinciaID', 'ProvinciaNombre', 'RegionID', 'ComunaID', 'ComunaNombre']
df_target = df_joined[['ProvinciaID', 'ProvinciaNombre', 'RegionID', 'ComunaID', 'ComunaNombre']]

# Ensure data types match target schema
df_target['ProvinciaID'] = df_target['ProvinciaID'].astype(int)
df_target['ProvinciaNombre'] = df_target['ProvinciaNombre'].astype(str)
df_target['RegionID'] = df_target['RegionID'].astype(int)
df_target['ComunaID'] = df_target['ComunaID'].astype(int)
df_target['ComunaNombre'] = df_target['ComunaNombre'].astype(str)

# Write the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_5/target_multisource.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_5/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_5/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source1_5_0 and Source1_5_1 on ProvinciaID
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="ProvinciaID", how="inner")

# Group by all columns (the full primary key) to ensure uniqueness and remove any duplicates
# Since the target examples have 172 tuples but join results in 173, grouping will remove duplicates
grouped = joined.groupby(
    ["ProvinciaID", "ProvinciaNombre", "RegionID", "ComunaID", "ComunaNombre"],
    as_index=False
).size()  # size() returns a Series with counts, but we don't need counts, so we drop it next

# The groupby.size() adds a count column, but we only want the grouped keys, so we drop the count column
# Instead, just do groupby with as_index=False and take first row per group
grouped = joined.groupby(
    ["ProvinciaID", "ProvinciaNombre", "RegionID", "ComunaID", "ComunaNombre"],
    as_index=False
).first()

# Write the final output with exact target schema column order
grouped = grouped[["ProvinciaID", "ProvinciaNombre", "RegionID", "ComunaID", "ComunaNombre"]]

grouped.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_5/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
